decisions.label: Figure 1
decisions.caption: UniWALM is a unified World Action Language Model that extends a single video-model backbone to act and reason by co-generating video, action, and language through unified attention.
decisions.reason: Teaser figure demonstrating the architectural shift from hybrid decoupled VLM+WAM to unified any-to-any WALM.

decisions.label: Figure 2
decisions.caption: Overview of UniWALM. UniWALM is a unified mixture-of-transformers (MoT) world-action-language model that co-denoises video, language, and action in a single shared representation.
decisions.reason: Crucial system architecture diagram showing VAE, T5, Proprio, Video DiT, Language DiT, Action DiT, and language memory loop.

decisions.label: Figure 3
decisions.caption: Flow Matching with Correction (FMC). A clean action x0 and its perturbed counterpart x0 + e1 are noised to the same time t. The model is trained to transport the perturbed sample back onto the clean trajectory.
decisions.reason: Core mathematical and geometric intuition for Flow Matching with Correction (FMC).

decisions.label: Figure 4
decisions.caption: Mixture of Transformers Layer. Each modality is processed by its own transformer that performs adaptive layer norm followed by Q,K,V projection and unified self-attention.
decisions.reason: Detailed micro-architecture of the MoT layer showing unified self-attention across (V|A|L) and cross-attention.

decisions.label: Figure 5
decisions.caption: Qualitative Results of UniWALM across simulation pick-and-place, find-the-item memory, simple dexterous, and complex bimanual removal.
decisions.reason: Qualitative execution gallery illustrating subtask reasoning and memory across diverse tasks.

decisions.label: Figure 6
decisions.caption: RMBench M(n) qualitative rollouts across Press Button, Battery Try, Blocks Ranking Try, and Cover Blocks.
decisions.reason: Qualitative evidence for memory-dependent tasks in RMBench demonstrating textual memory strings and subtasks.

decisions.label: Figure 7
decisions.caption: Language-as-memory loop on Press Button. At each step UniWALM emits a next subtask and textual memory that is re-consumed as prompt.
decisions.reason: Key visual demonstration of internal working memory state transitions (counters 0/3 to 3/3, 1/4 to 4/4) without external memory.

decisions.label: Figure 8
decisions.caption: Empty Container (real, bi-manual) rollouts. Each row is a successful UniWALM rollout showing bimanual coordination.
decisions.reason: Real-world bimanual dexterous manipulation execution rollouts.

decisions.label: Figure 9
decisions.caption: Real-world Find the Item rollouts under mid-episode occlusion and item shifting.
decisions.reason: Real-world memory validation showing preservation of spatial location mappings under occlusion.

decisions.label: Figure 10
decisions.caption: 2D robot-trajectory benchmark used for FMC ablation (Square, Spiral, Line, Figure-8).
decisions.reason: Benchmark shapes used to rigorously quantify trajectory drift and correction capability.

decisions.label: Figure 11
decisions.caption: FMC vs vanilla flow matching on 2D robot trajectories (overlay view). Blue curves are ground-truth; red are generated trajectories.
decisions.reason: Direct visual comparison proving FMC prevents trajectory truncation and mode collapse.

decisions.label: Figure 12
decisions.caption: Timing-lag failure on Press Button. Target counts are (left=5, middle=2, confirm=1); actual is 5-3-1 due to one-step late beta signal.
decisions.reason: Crucial negative result / error analysis illustrating physical execution overshoot despite correct textual memory.

decisions.label: Figure 13
decisions.caption: MolmoSpaces Pick & Place qualitative sequence showing subtask progression.
decisions.reason: Subsumed by Figure 5 and Figure 6 for concise layout; referenced in text.

decisions.label: Figure 14

decisions.reason: Subsumed by Figure 8 and Figure 9; referenced in text.
